title: Work-tape symbol after repeated walks
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $h$ index one of its work tapes, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. For any direction flag $neg$, Boolean flag $bl$, and natural number $a$, after $a$ repetitions of the simulated walk on tape $h$ in direction $neg$, the symbol scanned on that tape is the original tape content at the original head position shifted by $-a$ when $neg$ is true and by $a$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
h is a valid work-tape index
c is a configuration of M on x
neg and bl are Boolean flags
